evidence.artifact: template/programs/python/adversarial (Python adversarial/edge-case micro-program set for Section 17)
evidence.audit_method: Manual semantic review of every file against Section 17 hazard-category intent, cross-checked with targeted web verification of current CPython (3.10-3.14) runtime/parser behavior for the categories whose classification is version-sensitive. No execution was performed by this worker (packet-only, no local tools); this is a static/currency audit, not a re-measurement.
caveats: This audit is a static/semantic review only; no execution, compilation, or measurement was performed (packet-only worker, no local tools, and this is a currency audit rather than a re-measurement per the task Goal).

ADV-23.py's required binary input fixture (inputs/ADV-23.bin) was not part of the embedded packet and its content/UTF-8-validity could not be independently verified; the program logic itself is unaffected by toolchain currency.

Exact current MAXSTACK / parser-nesting threshold on the specific evaluated CPython build was not directly measured; the audit relies on the nesting depths chosen (1,000 and 10,000+) being far in excess of any documented or historically discussed MAXSTACK value, which is a safe margin.
evidence.overall_finding: All 32 embedded files remain syntactically parseable Python (except the three files that are intentionally malformed to test 'malformed source code' detection) and each program's semantics still map onto the hazard category it claims to test under a current mainstream CPython toolchain (3.10+). No file requires modification for continued validity.

per_file_notes.ADV-01_C.py / ADV-01_R.py: int64->int32 narrowing via ctypes.c_int32(large_value). ctypes truncation-on-construction behavior is stable and unchanged; still exercises silent narrowing.
per_file_notes.ADV-02_C.py / ADV-02_R.py: int64 overflow addition. Python ints are arbitrary-precision so no overflow occurs; this correctly demonstrates the language-specific absence of fixed-width overflow (a valid, intentional cross-language divergence, not a defect).
per_file_notes.ADV-03_C.py / ADV-03_R.py: Symmetric underflow case, same reasoning as ADV-02.
per_file_notes.ADV-04a_C.py / ADV-04a_R.py: Unsigned subtraction wraparound via ctypes.c_uint32; ctypes modular wraparound semantics unchanged.
per_file_notes.ADV-04b_C.py / ADV-04b_R.py: Signed/unsigned boundary comparison via ctypes; still valid.
per_file_notes.ADV-05_C.py / ADV-05_R.py: Out-of-range float->int32 via ctypes.c_int32(1e30); ctypes conversion behavior on out-of-range floats is stable.
per_file_notes.ADV-06_R.py / ADV-07_R.py: Float divide-by-zero + NaN self-inequality. Verified: current CPython still raises ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero for a/b with b==0.0 (confirmed via 2026-dated sources), so these programs will crash before reaching the NaN/self-eq print rather than silently producing inf/NaN. This is correct, unchanged Python semantics and a valid 'Runtime Safe Detection' classification target; not a defect in the artifact.
per_file_notes.ADV-08_C.py / ADV-08_R.py: Integer divide-by-zero via ctypes.c_int64; `//` with a zero divisor raises ZeroDivisionError, unchanged.
per_file_notes.ADV-09_C.py / ADV-09_R.py: Negative index access; Python's well-defined negative-indexing semantics (no lower-bound violation) still hold, correctly demonstrating a silent, language-specific 'transformation' of what other languages would treat as out-of-bounds.
per_file_notes.ADV-10_C.py / ADV-10_R.py: Positive out-of-range index (i=5 on a 5-element list) raises IndexError, unchanged.
per_file_notes.ADV-11_R.py: Huge allocation via list multiplication; behavior (MemoryError/OOM on huge n) unchanged.
per_file_notes.ADV-12.py: Reading an annotated-but-unassigned local (`v: ctypes.c_int64` with no value) raises UnboundLocalError; annotation-only binding semantics unchanged since introduced.
per_file_notes.ADV-13.py: typing.cast is a static-analysis no-op at runtime in all current CPython versions; the mis-cast silently succeeds and returns the real (wrong) attribute value, correctly modeling the 'invalid cast silently accepted' hazard.
per_file_notes.ADV-14_R.py: Type-hint-violating call (str passed where c_int64 hinted); Python does not enforce annotations at runtime in any current version, so `n * 3` on a str silently repeats the string. Confirmed still valid, unenforced-hint behavior.
per_file_notes.ADV-15.py: List mutation (append) during iteration; CPython's index-based list iterator still visits appended elements that fall within the growing length, producing iters=6/len=6. This iterator behavior is a long-stable CPython implementation detail and remains unchanged.
per_file_notes.ADV-16.py: Reassignment of an annotated variable; Python variable annotations were never enforced as immutability and this remains true in all current versions.
per_file_notes.ADV-17.py: Uses PEP 604 `str | None` syntax. <cite index="31-2">You can use the new syntax to replace Optional as well, which is what you used for type hinting that an argument could be None</cite>, and this syntax is natively usable since Python 3.10, so it remains valid on any current mainstream toolchain (3.10-3.14). len(None) still raises TypeError, unchanged.
per_file_notes.ADV-18.py: Missing-return branch; calling a function that implicitly returns None then multiplying by 2 raises TypeError, unchanged, and correctly exercises the 'missing return' hazard.
per_file_notes.ADV-19.py: Infinite recursion with no base case, relies on hitting Python's recursion limit. Verified current CPython's default recursion limit is still ~1000 (confirmed via multiple current, dated sources), so this still reliably raises RecursionError.
per_file_notes.ADV-20.py: Recursion to a fixed depth of 1,000,000 without adjusting sys.setrecursionlimit; since the default limit (~1000) is unchanged, this still reliably raises RecursionError before reaching the base case, correctly exercising 'excessive recursion depth.'
per_file_notes.ADV-21.py / ADV-21_depth1000.py / ADV-21: Extreme parenthesis nesting to test parser-stack limits. Verified via CPython issue trackers that deeply nested parenthesized/lambda expressions raise `MemoryError: Parser stack overflowed - Python source too complex to parse` from ast.parse/compile on current CPython, and that the parser's MAXSTACK threshold has been the subject of an active 3.14 regression/fix (gh-135028: nesting as shallow as ~200 could overflow before a targeted increase). <cite index="41-1">eval("(" * 200 + ")" * 200) ... MemoryError: Parser stack overflowed - Python source too complex to parse</cite>. Because all three files nest at nesting depths (1,000 / 10,000 / an even larger unnamed blob) far beyond any plausible current or historical MAXSTACK value, they remain reliable, deterministic triggers of a classifiable parse-time failure ('Compile-time Detection' family) rather than a silent success or an unclassifiable native crash on any current CPython release. No source change needed; if anything, current CPython is more likely than older releases to flag these at shallower depth, which only strengthens the test.
per_file_notes.ADV-22-valid.py / ADV-22a.py / ADV-22b.p: Baseline-valid vs. two intentionally malformed sources (truncated string literal; corrupted identifier via stray symbols) for 'malformed source code' detection. Both malformed variants remain SyntaxError-inducing on any current CPython tokenizer/parser; unchanged.
per_file_notes.ADV-23.py: Reads inputs/ADV-23.bin (malformed UTF-8 test); depends on an externally supplied binary fixture not embedded in this packet, presumed provided by the benchmark harness's input-fixture directory alongside the program. Nothing in the program's own logic (open().read() in text mode, len(s)) needs updating; text-mode decode-error semantics (UnicodeDecodeError on invalid UTF-8) are unchanged in current Python.
per_file_notes.ADV-24.py: Huge numeric literal (2^63+1) assigned to `int`; Python's arbitrary-precision int type has never had a literal-size ceiling relevant here (a large-int-to-str conversion length guard exists for str(int) on huge ints in very new CPython, but 9223372036854775809 is far too small to trigger it), so this remains valid and unaffected.
per_file_notes.ADV-25_R.py: External-input parsing (`int(input())`) then ctypes multiply; ValueError on non-numeric input is unchanged, correctly exercising 'invalid external input.'
per_file_notes.ADV-26_R.py: Standard binary-search boundary-value test; pure Python control flow, unaffected by any toolchain change.

toolchain_currency_checks_performed: Confirmed CPython's default recursion limit remains ~1000 in current releases (multiple 2025/2026-dated sources).
Confirmed float division by zero still raises ZeroDivisionError (not silent inf/NaN) in current CPython (2026-dated sources).
Confirmed PEP 604 `X | None` union syntax is natively valid since Python 3.10, safe for any current mainstream toolchain.

Confirmed CPython's PEG parser still raises a classifiable MemoryError ('Parser stack overflowed') on deeply nested parenthesized expressions rather than an unclassifiable crash, including noting an active 3.14-era MAXSTACK regression/fix (gh-135028) that only makes the ADV-21 family's very deep nesting more reliably diagnostic, not less.
